messages:
maria: Anyone else seeing a spike of 'no such host' from the GPU provisioner in ap-southeast? Started ~10:20 UTC, jobs failing to pull model manifests
tagging: logs show DNS NXDOMAIN when contacting internal model registry service

tom: Yep saw it. Node bringups failing w/ image pull-ish errors but dig shows DNS issues not containerd

jing: stacktrace clip: 
`error fetching model: Get https://models.internal-service.svc.cluster.local/manifest: dial tcp: lookup models.internal-service.svc.cluster.local: no such host`

maria: Key observations: only edge proxies in ap-southeast impacted, internal control-plane in eu-west fine. Failure pattern: short burst of NXDOMAIN then resolves after ~30s, repeats under load

dave: Could be split-horizon TTL mismatch between authoritative private DNS and the edge stub resolver cache. Edge uses local dnsmasq + systemd-resolved shim right?

maria: Correct. Edge proxy hosts: /etc/resolv.conf -> 127.0.0.53 (systemd-resolved) -> forwards to dnsmasq and then out to our VPC resolvers. ndots: 1, search path includes long svc.cluster.local entries

jing: Reproduced locally: `dig models.internal-service.svc.cluster.local @127.0.0.53` sometimes returns NXDOMAIN, sometimes RIGHT ANSWER, even when authoritative has A record.

maria: Dumped resolver cache on one host, found entries with very long negative TTL buckets. Looks like negative caching from an external forwarder got propagated with a TTL that conflicts with our split-horizon view

opsbot: deploy-bot: rolling restart requested for edge-proxy group ap-southeast (reason: transient DNS failures). :gear:

tom: Quick mitigation: restart systemd-resolved on edge-proxies to clear negative cache. Also temporarily drop search path to avoid triggering ndots search fanout.

jing: Command we ran: 
```
sudo systemctl restart systemd-resolved
sudo ln -sf /run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf /etc/resolv.conf
# temporarily set /etc/resolv.conf to use local dnsmasq explicitly
```

maria: After restart, provisioning stabilised for ~15m but failure popped again when load increased. Hypothesis: resolver rotation to an external forwarder (egress NAT IP pool) hit a noisy forwarder that was returning NXDOMAIN for split view names (maybe DNS64/NAT translation or a firewall) and our stub cached the negative result

dave: If the forwarder is outside our split-horizon, it may legitimately not know internal names and reply SERVFAIL/NXDOMAIN. Negative caching semantics (RFC 2308) allow caching of NXDOMAIN for the provided TTL. Some forwarders set very long negative TTLs (900s+). Under high concurrency we'll slam the same forwarder and suffer a thundering negative cache effect

maria: Action items I pushed:
- Add a resolv policy to prefer internal resolvers for kube svc domains (split-horizon predicate)
- Shorten negative cache TTL at the dnsmasq layer (`neg-ttl=5`) on edges
- Add probe that runs `dig` against authoritative edge forwarder every minute and alerts on NXDOMAIN spikes

tom: Also let's increase ndots to 5? That'll actually increase search attempts and could make it worse. Better: reduce search path length and ensure clients send FQDNs (stop relying on search). We can enforce FQDN in model fetch URLs from provisioner code quickly

jing: Submitted PR to provisioner to always use FQDN for internal model endpoints and to backoff on DNS failures (exponential backoff 250ms -> 2s). PR: https://git.internal/redwood/provisioner/pull/1123

maria: SRE note: We traced that the noisy forwarder belongs to cloud provider region egress pool 10.240.8.0/24; opening ticket with cloud to get it quarantined

sre-oncall: Put a temporary route policy to prefer internal resolvers for traffic from edge-proxies to 10.1.2.3 (private-authoritative). Also tagging a runbook entry: if NXDOMAIN spike > 5% for 5m, restart systemd-resolved and notify infra oncall

dave: Postmortem checklist: verify negative ttl at each layer (client stub, dnsmasq, systemd-resolved), add unit tests for client code to use FQDNs, and add dashboards for negative-cache spikes per region

maria: TL;DR: transient NXDOMAINs from an external forwarder caused negative caching on edge stubs which led to GPU node provisioning thrash. Mitigations in progress: force FQDNs, reduce neg-ttl on edges, prefer internal authoritative resolvers, and cloud ticket for noisy forwarder. Will follow up if the cloud quarantines the IP range.
